label: AQ 0026
title: The plan that knew the ending

questions.q: Why not have people write the plans?
questions.a: Scale and cost. Plan-and-Act calls collecting plans by hand “costly and time-consuming”; it generated 15,000 synthetic examples with GPT-4o in under an hour, against “days or weeks” to collect as many trajectories. I'd still have people plan a small sample, to audit the synthetic plans for steps nobody could know in advance.

questions.q: Isn't hindsight relabelling a standard, safe trick?
questions.a: For instructions, yes. NNetNav (Murty et al., 2024) lets an agent explore websites, then labels each run with the instruction it fulfils; Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuned on 10,000 such demonstrations reached over 16% success on WebArena. My reasoning: an instruction is the input and the run really carries it out. A plan is the output, written before the run, so hindsight there leaks.

teach.title: How it works: building the set without the leak

questions.q: How would you tell whether a trained planner picked up the leak?
questions.a: My suggestions: on held-out tasks, count plan steps naming specific things absent from the task and first screen. Then change the site (a new top contributor, a moved file) and rerun; a leaky planner writes the old facts confidently.

teach.title: How it works: building the set without the leak

questions.q: What did Plan-and-Act ask its teacher model to do with each trajectory?
questions.a: Read a successful web-agent trajectory and “reverse-engineer” a structured plan from it, saying which actions belong to which plan step. Plans written without the trajectory didn't match the real website.

teach.title: How it works: building the set without the leak

questions.q: Why does a plan written after the run leak, when an instruction written after the run is fine?
questions.a: An instruction is the input, and the run really does what it says. A plan is the target the planner must write from the task and first screen alone, so facts found mid-run (a name, a file) teach it to invent them.

teach.title: How it works: building the set without the leak

questions.q: In Plan-and-Act's table that adds one piece at a time, what did replanning add on WebArena-Lite?
questions.a: With the fine-tuned executor and synthetic trajectories, success on these web tasks rose from 43.63% to 53.94%, a 10.31-point gain, the largest step for that executor.
